query: What signals suggest an incident will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorising incidents by type gives a genuine grouping axis for comparing resolution time across categories. Values align well with short_description (VPN->vpn, database->database, email->email). Note original table has a 'category' column, but this appears to be a finer text-derived categorisation, not a trivial duplicate.

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: Failure mode is a plausibly strong predictor of resolution effort (outage vs sync vs crash), giving a new modelling axis. Values are mostly warranted readings ('Cannot connect'->connection_failure). The 'Email system not working properly'->service_outage is a somewhat generous inference but defensible; NULLs for silent rows are acceptable.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Blast radius (individual vs department-wide vs server-side) is highly relevant to resolution time. Department_wide and location_specific are well grounded when text names a department. However 'server_side'/'individual_user' for texts like 'Cannot connect to database' or 'Email system not working properly' are inferred without explicit textual support, introducing some ungrounded specificity.

per_column.name: assignment_lag
per_column.rationale: Whether assignment was delayed is a plausible predictor of longer resolution, and the boolean is well balanced (non-constant). However groundedness is uncertain: the samples only expose closed_at/sys_updated_on, and the derivation of a lag boolean (needing opened_at/assignment timing) cannot be verified from the evidence shown; the flag reads 'False' even for rows with no visible timing gap, so the basis is unclear.

per_column.name: assigned_equals_closed_by
per_column.rationale: Comparing assigned_to to closed_by (handoff indicator) is a reasonable signal for resolution complexity and is directly derivable from two original columns. Slightly lower usefulness as it is a simple equality of existing fields, but it does add a new comparative axis. NULLs for unclosed rows are correct.

per_column.name: caller_type
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing itil_user vs named_user could correlate with resolution behaviour, giving a modest grouping axis. Derivability from caller_id/sys fields is plausible but not directly shown in the evidence samples, so groundedness is moderate.

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: Agent identity is a legitimate axis for resolution-time analysis, but it substantially overlaps with the existing 'assigned_to' original column, so it is largely a normalised restatement. Values (Beth_Anglin, Fred_Luddy, etc.) are consistent with an assignment field and 'unassigned' is handled reasonably.

judge.rationale: The added columns give several genuine new axes (category, failure_mode, scope, assignment handoff/lag) directly relevant to predicting longer resolution, with only mild redundancy (assigned_agent vs assigned_to) and one near-duplicate of the original category column. Groundedness is generally sound for text-extracted fields, with the main weaknesses being (a) inferred scope/failure values that add specificity beyond what terse descriptions state, and (b) assignment_lag/caller_type whose derivation is not verifiable from the exposed source fields. No outright fabrications or contradictions observed, and NULLs are used appropriately.
